The photo editor has sliders for exposure and color, crop and resize tools, and a large set of filters and effects. A collage maker arranges photos into layouts, and the graphic designer tool offers templates for social media posts, flyers, and cards. Everything runs in a web page, with mobile access too.

AI tools handle common edits. An enhancer sharpens and improves photos, a background remover cuts out subjects, and retouching tools smooth skin and remove blemishes. Artistic effects turn photos into paintings or cartoons, and an upscaler increases resolution. Newer features add AI image generation and a way to remove objects. Many of these are one-click operations, which is the main appeal.

item.title: Biteable
item.description:
Biteable makes video creation approachable for non-editors. Users pick a template for something like a company announcement, training clip, or social promo, and replace text, images, and footage scene by scene. Brand settings keep colors, fonts, and logos consistent across a team.

AI features accelerate the first draft. A script or prompt can generate a sequence of scenes with suggested visuals, text can be turned into narration, and videos can be resized for formats such as vertical social posts and widescreen. Collaboration features let teammates review and edit, and analytics show how videos perform.

item.title: Boomy
item.description: Boomy is one of the easiest ways to generate music. You pick a style such as lo-fi, electronic, rap beats, or cinematic, and the system composes a track in moments. You can then adjust it by changing the arrangement, adding vocals or effects, and recording your own voice over the music. It requires no musical knowledge, which is why it appeals to casual creators and people who want custom background tracks.

item.title: Brandmark
item.description:
Brandmark makes logo design accessible to people without a designer. You type a name and tagline, choose keywords, colors, and styles you like, and its algorithms generate many logo concepts that combine icons, fonts, and layouts. You can edit the colors, fonts, and arrangement, and see how the logo looks on mockups such as business cards and websites.

Rather than a subscription, Brandmark sells one-time packages. The basic package includes a logo in standard file formats, and higher tiers add vector files, social media graphics, a brand style guide, business card templates, and the right to use the design commercially. The vector files can be edited in design software, and the packages focus on getting a usable identity quickly.

item.title: Canva
item.description: For infographics, Canva works as a template-first editor. You choose a layout for a process, timeline, comparison, statistic, or report, then replace the placeholder text and swap in your own colors and fonts. The element library supplies icons, illustrations, shapes, and photos, and chart tools let you paste or upload numbers to draw bar charts, pie charts, and other graphs that update when the data changes. Because it is a drag-and-drop tool, people without design training can produce something tidy in under an hour.

item.title: Canva
item.description: Canva is a design tool for people who are not designers. You start from a template, swap in your own text and photos, and export the result, which cuts out most of the layout decisions that make design software hard to learn. It covers social media posts, presentations, flyers, resumes, posters, short videos, whiteboards, and simple websites in one editor. A built-in library of photos, graphics, fonts, and music means most projects can be finished without leaving the app.

item.title: Captions AI
item.description: Captions is built for creators who film themselves speaking. You record or upload a video, and it transcribes the speech and adds stylish animated captions, which is important because many people watch social video with the sound off. It can remove filler words and silences, cut the video into a tighter version, and add zooms and effects that keep viewers watching. It works well on a phone, which suits creators who edit as they go.

item.title: Charisma.ai
item.description:
Charisma.ai helps creators combine writing with generative AI. Instead of leaving a character entirely to a language model, creators design a story with scenes, goals, and character personalities, and the platform lets characters respond flexibly to what players say while steering the conversation along the intended narrative. This approach aims to keep stories coherent and on message, which is a common problem with free-form AI dialogue.

Tools include a visual story editor, character memory and emotion systems, voice and animation integration, and SDKs for Unity, Unreal, and web apps. The platform has been used for games, interactive entertainment, branded experiences, and training simulations where conversation practice is valuable. Writers can control tone and limits while still giving players freedom.

item.title: Civitai
item.description:
Civitai is where much of the open-source image generation community meets. Creators upload checkpoints, LoRAs, embeddings, and other add-ons for Stable Diffusion, FLUX, and related models, together with sample images and the prompts used. Others download them to run locally in tools like ComfyUI or Automatic1111, or try them in the browser. Ratings, comments, and example galleries make it easier to judge a model before downloading.

The site offers more than a library. Users can generate images on Civitai’s servers using credits, train their own LoRAs from a set of images, and take part in challenges and bounties that reward creators. Articles and guides share techniques, and a point system pays for the use of the site’s services. It became the unofficial catalog for community-trained styles, characters, and concepts.

item.title: Cleanfeed
item.description:
Cleanfeed lets people record or broadcast audio over the internet without installing software. A host creates a session, guests join by link in a browser, and the platform streams audio with low delay and records each participant on a separate track. It is popular with radio and podcast teams who need dependable quality.

The audio chain is a focus. It offers a noise gate, level controls, and processing options that tidy up voices, plus connections for studio equipment and phone callers. Producers can monitor and route audio, record backups, and download multitrack files. A newer version improves collaboration and integration with video.

item.title: Cleanup.pictures
item.description:
Cleanup.pictures does one thing with minimal effort. Upload a photo, brush over a stranger in the background, a power line, a logo, or a blemish, and the tool removes it and fills the gap with a plausible background. Results come back within seconds and can be downloaded, which makes it a quick fix for product photos, real estate listings, travel pictures, and social media posts.

It works well on simple backgrounds such as sky, grass, walls, and water, and less well when the removed object sits in front of detailed patterns, faces, or text that the model would have to invent. For larger images, a higher-resolution output is available on paid plans. The same kind of inpainting appears in other tools, including Clipdrop, which offers a related cleanup feature, along with Photoshop’s Generative Fill and Remove tool and the Magic Eraser on Google Pixel phones.

item.title: Clideo
item.description:
Clideo offers simple video tools that run in the browser. A user uploads a clip, picks a tool such as trimming, merging, compressing, resizing, or converting formats, and downloads the result. The pitch is convenience for quick jobs where installing editing software is not worth it.

AI features add some automation. Auto subtitles transcribe speech and add styled captions in many languages, and background removal and other effects help prepare clips for social media. The editor handles basic timeline work, and tools for audio, GIFs, and screen recording are included in the suite.

item.title: Colossyan
item.description: Colossyan targets companies that need a lot of video for learning and communication but do not want to film each one. You type or paste a script, or upload a document or slides and have it converted, choose an AI presenter and voice, and Colossyan produces a video. Editing works like slides, with scenes, text, images, and screen recordings, and changing the script means regenerating the video instead of reshooting.

item.title: ComfyUI
item.description: ComfyUI gives you precise control over generative AI by showing the whole pipeline. Instead of a prompt box and a button, you assemble a graph: load a model, encode a prompt, set up a sampler, add LoRAs or ControlNet for guidance, upscale, and save. Each step is a node you can inspect and rewire. It started with Stable Diffusion and now supports many image, video, and audio models, including FLUX, so new models are often usable in ComfyUI first.

item.title: Craiyon
item.description:
Craiyon began as DALL-E mini, an open-source experiment that went viral for producing odd, low-resolution images from text prompts. It was one of the first image generators many people tried, and it popularized the idea that anyone could make pictures with words. The site then rebranded as Craiyon and kept its low barrier to entry: open the page, type a prompt, and wait for the results.

The quality has improved with newer models, and Craiyon now produces more detailed images in several styles, including photos, illustrations, and drawings. Paid plans remove ads, speed up generation, and add features such as faster queues, higher resolution, and a private mode. The tool is positioned for casual use, like quick illustrations, memes, and idea sketches, instead of professional production.

item.title: D-ID
item.description:
D-ID became known for animating still photos. You upload a portrait and add a script or audio, and the platform produces a video in which the person appears to speak, with lip movement and facial expressions. That idea grew into a full avatar platform: a studio where you create presenters, choose voices and languages, and generate videos for training, marketing, and customer communication.

Beyond videos, D-ID provides tools for interactive use. An API lets developers generate talking avatars in their own applications, and real-time agents combine an avatar, a language model, and a voice so that a digital person can hold a conversation on a website or kiosk. The company also works on privacy technology, with its origins in tools that protect faces from recognition systems.

item.title: Descript
item.description:
Descript changed how many people edit podcasts and videos. After recording, Descript transcribes the audio, and deleting a word from the transcript cuts it from the media. That makes editing feel like working in a document, which is friendlier for people without video editing experience.

AI tools extend the idea. Studio Sound improves audio quality in one click, filler word removal cleans speech, eye contact correction adjusts gaze, and the underlord assistant performs edits from instructions. Voice cloning lets you fix a word by typing it, and text can drive screen recording, multi-track editing, and clips for social media.

item.title: Descript
item.description: Descript changed how many people edit audio and video. You upload a recording, it produces a transcript, and you cut, rearrange, and delete the media by editing the text like a document. Removing a sentence in the transcript removes it from the recording. For podcasts, interviews, tutorials, and talking-head videos, that is much faster than working on a waveform, and people who have never used an editor can pick it up quickly.

item.title: Descript Studio Sound
item.description:
Studio Sound targets the common problem of recording in imperfect spaces. Apply it to a clip in Descript, and the AI removes noise, reduces echo and reverb, and evens out the voice, making recordings made on a laptop or phone sound much more professional. It works on a whole project or a selected portion and has an intensity setting, so you can balance cleanup against natural sound.

It is built into Descript’s editing workflow, so you can clean audio while editing the transcript, and it works on both audio and video projects. Podcasters, interviewers, educators, and video creators use it to rescue recordings from noisy environments. It can be combined with other features in Descript, such as filler word removal and eye contact correction for video.

item.title: Dolby.io
item.description:
Dolby.io brings Dolby’s audio expertise to developers as web services. A developer sends an audio or video file and receives a processed version: cleaner speech, reduced background noise, balanced loudness, or improved dialogue. These APIs fit podcast tools, video platforms, and conferencing products.

Other parts of the platform focus on real-time streaming. Millicast delivers low-latency video to large audiences, which suits live events, interactive broadcasts, and remote production. Analysis and transcoding APIs help prepare content for different devices.

item.title: Dream by WOMBO
item.description: Dream by WOMBO is aimed at casual creators who want to see their ideas as art without learning prompt techniques. You type a phrase, pick a style such as oil painting, anime, fantasy, or neon, and the app returns an image in a few seconds. The style menu does much of the work that detailed prompts would do in other tools, which makes it approachable on a phone. It is popular for profile pictures, wallpapers, and quick social posts.

item.title: Elai.io
item.description:
Elai.io is aimed at people who need a presenter video without filming. A user picks from a library of avatars, enters a script or imports a document, selects a voice and language, and the platform produces a video of the avatar speaking. Backgrounds, text, and media can be added in a slide-like editor.

Typical uses are training videos, product explainers, and marketing content, and the ability to translate into many languages helps localize quickly. Custom avatars can be created from a person’s footage. Features such as converting articles or links into videos speed up content creation.

item.title: ElevenLabs
item.description:
ElevenLabs is known for natural-sounding synthetic speech. Users type text and choose a voice, or clone a voice from a sample, and get audio that carries intonation and emotion. The platform supports dozens of languages and accents and offers a library of voices.

Its products now span several uses. Dubbing translates video into other languages while keeping the speaker’s voice, audiobook and narration tools produce long-form audio, and a conversational agent platform builds voice assistants that talk with customers in real time. Music and sound effect generation, plus speech to text, round out the suite. An API lets developers embed these features.

item.title: ElevenLabs
item.description: ElevenLabs is best known for text-to-speech that sounds like a person rather than a robot. You paste in a script, choose a voice from a large library or make your own, and the tool reads it with natural pacing and emotion. The same voice can speak dozens of languages, which makes it a popular option for audiobooks, YouTube narration, e-learning, game characters, and accessibility. Voice cloning builds a copy of a voice from a recording, and there are safeguards around it: you are meant to have the speaker’s permission, and some features require identity checks.

item.title: ElevenLabs Sound Effects
item.description:
ElevenLabs Sound Effects creates audio from a sentence. You describe the sound you need, such as a door creaking in an empty house or a crowd cheering in a stadium, and the model generates several options in seconds, which you can adjust for length and download. This helps video editors, game developers, podcasters, and filmmakers who otherwise search libraries for the right clip or record effects themselves.

The company also offers a Voice Isolator that separates speech from background noise and music, helping clean up interviews and field recordings. These tools fit alongside ElevenLabs’ text-to-speech, dubbing, and music features, so a creator can produce a full soundtrack in one place. An API allows developers to generate effects inside apps and games.

item.title: Figma
item.description: Figma is where a lot of software gets designed before anyone writes code. It runs in the browser, so designers, product managers, engineers, and writers can open the same file at once, leave comments, and watch changes appear live. That ended the old habit of emailing design files back and forth. Its core strengths are vector editing, Auto Layout for components that resize correctly, and shared libraries that keep colors, type, and buttons consistent across a whole product.

item.title: Filmora AI
item.description:
Filmora sits between simple phone apps and professional suites. It offers a timeline editor with effects, titles, transitions, and a large library of templates and stock assets, with a design aimed at beginners and hobbyists.

AI features automate tedious work. Smart cutout removes backgrounds from video, noise removal cleans audio, speech-to-text creates captions, and a text-based editor lets users cut by editing the transcript. Generative tools add music, images, and effects.

item.title: FlexClip
item.description:
FlexClip is a browser-based video maker for people without editing experience. You start from a template or a blank timeline, drop in clips, images, text, and music from its stock library, and trim and arrange them with drag and drop. It exports in common formats and sizes for social platforms, and includes screen and webcam recording for tutorials. It is used by small businesses, teachers, and social media managers.

AI features speed up production. Text-to-video builds a draft from a script or idea, an AI script writer drafts the narration, and auto subtitles transcribe speech and add captions in many languages. Background removal for video, text-to-speech voiceovers, and AI image generation fill other gaps. Some features turn a blog post or product page into a video, which marketers use for repurposing content.

item.title: Fliki
item.description:
Fliki turns written content into video. A user pastes a script, links an article, or writes a prompt, and the tool splits it into scenes, picks visuals from a stock library or generated media, and adds narration with a synthetic voice. The editor allows swapping clips, adjusting text, and changing voices.

A big draw is the range of voices and languages, which lets creators produce the same video in several markets. Avatars and voice cloning are available, and text to speech is offered as a standalone product for narration and audio. Marketers, educators, and YouTubers use it to repurpose content.

item.title: Freepik AI
item.description: Freepik began as a stock site for vectors, photos, and icons, and many designers already knew it. It has added a full AI suite on top. The image generator creates pictures from text prompts, and tools for editing, upscaling, retouching, and expanding images let users refine them. Video generation and animation features turn stills or prompts into short clips, and a workspace organizes projects and lets you mix different tools.

item.title: Gen-2
item.description:
Runway builds generative video tools for filmmakers, designers, and creators. Gen-3 Alpha was a major step in its line, generating short clips from a text prompt or an image with better detail, motion, and consistency than earlier versions. It supported controls for camera movement and style.

Runway’s platform around its models includes editing tools, motion brush features, and ways to extend or modify clips. Its research focuses on world models and video generation for creative work, and the company works with studios and artists. The newer models in the line have largely taken the place of Gen-3.

item.title: Generated Photos
item.description:
Generated Photos solves a licensing problem: real people’s faces carry privacy and consent obligations, and stock photos can be expensive or restrictive. Its library holds images of faces created by generative models, which depict nobody in particular. Designers use them for website and app mockups, marketers for illustrations, and developers for placeholder avatars in user interfaces.

Several tools extend the library. A face generator lets you pick attributes such as age, gender, ethnicity, hair, and emotion and create new faces, and a photo anonymizer replaces a real face in a picture with a synthetic one. Datasets of synthetic faces serve machine learning teams who need varied images without privacy concerns, and an API provides access for automated use. Full-body and other synthetic image options have been added.

item.title: GetIMG.ai
item.description: getimg.ai provides a web workspace for creating and editing images with AI. You can generate pictures from a prompt using a choice of models, including Stable Diffusion variants and other leading generators, then refine them. Tools for inpainting let you replace part of an image, outpainting extends it past its borders, and an infinite canvas allows you to compose scenes from several generations. Upscaling, background removal, and face tools help finish the result.

item.title: HeyGen
item.description: HeyGen lets you make a talking-head video without filming. You choose an avatar or create your own from a short recording, paste or write a script, and HeyGen generates a video with natural speech and lip movement. It supports dozens of languages, and one of its popular uses is video translation: upload a video of yourself, and it produces a version in another language with your voice and matching lip movements. Marketers, trainers, and sales teams use it to produce content quickly.

item.title: Homestyler
item.description:
Homestyler makes home design accessible. You draw a floor plan or start from a template, add walls, doors, and windows, and then furnish rooms from a catalog of real products and styles. A 3D view lets you walk through the space, and realistic renderings show how finishes and lighting would look. Homeowners use it to plan renovations and arrange furniture, and designers use it to present ideas to clients.

AI features speed up design. Tools can generate interior styles from a photo of a room, suggest layouts, and produce renderings from a simple description, and some features let you scan or upload a room as a starting point. Community galleries share designs for inspiration, and links to retailers make it easier to buy items you have selected.

item.title: Houzz
item.description:
Houzz started as a place to browse home photos and save ideas. Users look through millions of images of kitchens, bathrooms, gardens, and living rooms, save them to idea books, and find the products and professionals behind them. A directory lists architects, designers, and contractors with reviews and portfolios, so homeowners can contact people who match their taste and budget.

The platform includes a marketplace for furniture, lighting, and home goods, with augmented reality features that show how an item might look in your room. For professionals, Houzz Pro is software for managing leads, estimates, invoices, projects, and client communication, with tools to showcase their work. AI features help with design suggestions, image search, and automating parts of the business workflow.

item.title: Imgflip
item.description:
Imgflip makes memes easy. Users pick from a large library of templates, add text, and download or share the result. Other tools on the site include GIF makers, a meme gallery, and custom template uploads, and the community creates and votes on content.

The AI meme generator speeds up the creative step. A user describes a topic or mood, and the tool chooses a template and writes captions, which can then be edited. People use it for social media, group chats, and marketing that leans on humor.

item.title: Infogram
item.description:
Infogram helps turn numbers into visual stories. You choose a template for an infographic, report, chart, or dashboard, import data from a spreadsheet or connect to a live source, and customize the design with your brand colors and fonts. The tool produces polished charts and maps, many of them interactive, that can be embedded on websites or shared as links.

Several features support data communication. Over thirty chart types, including maps and tables, handle different kinds of data, and live data connections update visuals when the source changes. Teams can collaborate on projects, keep brand templates, and publish with analytics. Downloads include images and PDFs, and AI features help generate visuals and suggest ways to present data.

item.title: InVideo
item.description:
InVideo targets creators and marketers who need many videos fast. In InVideo AI, you describe the video you want, such as a product explainer, a faceless YouTube video, or a social ad, and it writes a script, selects stock clips, adds a voiceover and music, and assembles it. You can then give plain-language instructions to change scenes, tone, or length, which makes iteration quick for people without editing skills.

The traditional editor remains for more control. It provides templates, a timeline, text and effects, and a large stock library, and it can turn blog posts and scripts into videos. Voice features include text-to-speech in many languages and voice cloning, and recent versions have added AI-generated video clips and avatars alongside stock footage. Exports are available in formats for different social platforms.

item.title: InVision
item.description:
InVision was one of the leading prototyping and design collaboration tools of the 2010s. Designers uploaded static screens, linked them into clickable prototypes, and shared them with stakeholders for feedback. It also offered a design system manager and, later, Freehand, a collaborative whiteboard.

As Figma and other tools took over design work, InVision’s usage declined, and the company announced it would close its products. Teams moved their work to other platforms, and exports were offered for a period before shutdown.

item.title: Inworld AI
item.description:
Inworld AI began by giving non-player characters in games personality, memory, and the ability to converse. Developers define a character’s background, goals, and knowledge, and the platform handles dialogue, emotion, and behavior using language models, so players can talk to characters freely instead of choosing from scripted options. Integrations with Unity and Unreal Engine make it easy to add to games.

The company has evolved toward infrastructure for real-time AI applications. Its runtime helps developers build and scale voice and conversational experiences with low latency, and it offers text-to-speech models and tools for combining speech recognition, language models, and voice into agents. Use cases extend from games to training simulations, companions, and consumer apps with talking characters.

item.title: iZotope RX
item.description:
RX is the tool engineers reach for when audio is flawed. Its spectral display shows sound as an image, making it possible to see and remove specific problems, such as a cough, a phone buzz, or a chair squeak, without affecting the rest. Modules cover denoising, de-clicking, de-hum, de-reverb, de-clipping, and other repair tasks, and are used by post-production teams, podcast producers, forensic analysts, and musicians.

Machine learning powers its newer tools. Dialogue Isolate separates speech from background sounds, Music Rebalance lets you adjust the levels of vocals, bass, and drums in a finished mix, and Spectral Recovery restores high frequencies lost in low-quality files. Dialogue Contour and other features help produce consistent speech. It works as a standalone editor and as plugins in digital audio workstations and video editors.

item.title: Kaedim
item.description:
Kaedim addresses a slow stage in game and digital content production: turning concept art into 3D assets. You upload an image of a character, prop, or environment piece, and Kaedim produces a 3D model that matches it. The aim is to give artists a solid starting point they can refine, which cuts down the days of modeling work needed for each asset.

The service has been known for mixing machine learning with human review. Models go through checks by 3D artists who clean up errors before they are delivered, which improves reliability compared with fully automatic generators, but may slow turnaround. Output can be downloaded in common formats and used in engines like Unity and Unreal or imported into Blender and Maya for editing. Teams use it for game props, virtual production, and prototyping product ideas.

item.title: Kapwing
item.description:
Kapwing is an online editor aimed at creators and teams who need fast, polished content. You upload video or start from a template, trim, add captions, music, and effects, and export in formats suited to platforms such as TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube. Because it runs in the browser, there is nothing to install, and collaborators can work in the same project and leave comments.

AI features are at the center of the workflow. Auto subtitles transcribe speech and add stylized captions in many languages, background removal works without a green screen, and tools can remove silences and filler words, translate and dub videos, and clean up audio. A repurposing tool cuts long videos into short clips for social media, and text-to-video and script features help generate drafts. Brand kits keep fonts and colors consistent.

item.title: Krisp
item.description: Krisp installs as a virtual microphone and speaker, so it sits between your hardware and whatever calling app you use. It removes noise before it reaches the other person: barking dogs, keyboard clatter, traffic, and other voices in the room. It can also clean incoming audio, so a participant on a bad connection or in a loud space sounds clearer to you. Because it works with Zoom, Teams, Meet, Slack, and nearly any other app, one setup covers all of them.

item.title: LANDR
item.description:
LANDR started with automated mastering. An artist uploads a mixed song, the system analyzes it, and an algorithm applies equalization, compression, and loudness adjustments, producing a master in minutes at a price below hiring an engineer. Style and loudness options guide the result.

The company now offers a wider set of services for independent musicians: distribution to streaming platforms, a marketplace of samples, plugins, a collaboration network, and tools for mixing and creating. A subscription bundles many of these.

item.title: Lensa AI
item.description:
Lensa is a mobile photo editor best known for a single viral feature. Magic Avatars let users upload a set of selfies and receive a collection of stylized portraits in the style of fantasy art, anime, or illustration. The effect spread quickly on social media, driving downloads and making many people aware of AI image generation. The avatars are created with a model fine-tuned on each user’s photos.

The core of the app is a selfie and portrait editor. It offers retouching for skin and eyes, background replacement, blur and sharpening, and a range of filters and effects. Subscribers get access to the full tool set, and Magic Avatars can be purchased as packs. Prisma Labs, the developer, also makes other photo and AI apps.

item.title: LogoAI
item.description:
LogoAI creates logo options from a short brief. A user enters a name, picks an industry and styles they like, and the tool generates a set of designs. They can customize colors, fonts, and layouts, and download vector files and brand assets.

Small businesses and startups use it for a fast start on branding. Packages include business cards, social media graphics, and brand guidelines. The vector output can be used in print and on the web.

item.title: Looka
item.description:
Looka makes logo design approachable. You answer a few questions about your business, choose styles and colors you like, and Looka generates many logo concepts using different icons, fonts, and layouts. You can customize any option in an editor, then see how it looks on mockups such as business cards, signs, and social media profiles.

It offers two ways to pay. A one-time purchase of a logo package provides high-resolution and vector files, and a subscription Brand Kit adds a library of templates, a style guide, and tools for marketing materials, business cards, and social posts in your brand colors. It also includes a simple website builder, so a new business can establish a basic presence in one place.

item.title: Loom
item.description:
Loom replaces many meetings and long emails with a short video. You click record, show your screen while talking, and Loom uploads the video instantly and gives you a link to share. Viewers can watch at their own pace, react with emojis, comment at specific timestamps, and get an automatic transcript. It’s widely used for product walkthroughs, bug reports, onboarding, feedback, and updates to distributed teams.

AI features cut the work around videos. Loom creates titles and summaries, chapters for easy navigation, and action items, and can remove filler words and silences or turn a recording into a written document or ticket. Integrations connect with Slack, Jira, Notion, and Gmail, and since Atlassian acquired Loom, it fits more closely with tools like Jira and Confluence.

item.title: Lottie
item.description: Lottie is an animation format created at Airbnb that exports motion from After Effects as small JSON files. The files are vector-based, so they scale to any size without blur, and they are far lighter than GIFs or videos. App and web developers use them for loading spinners, onboarding screens, icons, and illustrations. A Lottie animation can be changed in code, colors can be swapped, and playback controlled, which makes it interactive.

item.title: Loudly
item.description:
Loudly offers music for people who need soundtracks without composing. Users can create tracks by choosing a genre, mood, and tempo, or by describing what they want in a prompt, and then download the result. A library of ready-made AI tracks lets you browse by genre and use case. It is intended for video creators, podcasters, streamers, game developers, and businesses that need background music.

Several features support practical use. A personalization option adjusts elements like instruments and structure, stems can be downloaded for editing, and an API allows developers to embed music generation in their own products, such as apps that need adaptive soundtracks. The company positions its music as safe for commercial use, with licenses that cover content on social platforms.

item.title: Lucidchart AI
item.description:
Lucidchart is a mature online diagramming tool from Lucid Software. Users create flowcharts, process maps, org charts, wireframes, network diagrams, and technical drawings with a large library of shapes and templates, and collaborate in real time with comments and version history. Because it runs in the browser and integrates with the tools that teams already use, it’s popular in business and IT.

Several features go beyond drawing. Data linking can generate org charts or network diagrams from spreadsheets and cloud accounts, so diagrams stay current, and a presentation mode turns diagrams into slides. AI features generate diagrams from a text description, suggest improvements, and summarize complex drawings. Lucidchart is part of the Lucid suite, which also includes Lucidspark for whiteboarding and Lucidscale for cloud diagrams.

item.title: Ludo.ai
item.description:
Ludo.ai aims to speed up the early stages of game development. Designers can brainstorm game concepts and mechanics, get suggestions based on trends in app stores, and generate descriptions and feature lists. A market research tool analyzes top-performing games to show what genres and themes are popular, which helps indie studios and publishers decide what to build.

The platform includes asset generation. It can produce concept art and character designs, sprites and sprite sheets, short animations, UI elements, and sound effects and music from prompts, and convert images into basic 3D models in some plans. Outputs are intended for prototypes and mockups to test ideas quickly, and can be exported for use in engines like Unity.

item.title: Luma AI
item.description:
Luma began in 3D. Its first app let anyone capture an object or space with a phone camera and turn it into a photorealistic 3D scene using neural radiance fields and, later, Gaussian splatting. People used it to scan products, rooms, and sculptures, and share them in a browser or export them to 3D tools. It also released Genie, a text-to-3D model that creates 3D assets from a description.

The company has since shifted its attention to video and multimodal generation. Its Ray video models create clips from text or images, and tools for editing existing footage, keyframes, and reframing give creators control. These models are available through the Dream Machine app and an API. Luma has also introduced agents that plan and carry out creative work across text, images, video, and audio, and it works with studios on production workflows.

item.title: Mage.space
item.description:
Mage.space gives people a simple front end for open-source image models. You choose from a catalog of checkpoints, write a prompt, adjust settings like style, size, and number of images, and generate. It supports image-to-image transformations, inpainting, and control features that guide composition, and results can be upscaled. Because it hosts the models, users do not need a powerful computer or a local installation.

The platform appeals to people who want flexibility in styles, from realistic photos to anime and fantasy art, and who want to experiment with community-trained models. It has a gallery of public creations, and a text-to-video tool has been added to some plans. Content rules are looser than on some mainstream services, though it still prohibits illegal material.

item.title: Masterpiece Studio
item.description:
Masterpiece Studio began with virtual reality tools for sculpting, painting, and animating in 3D, making 3D creation more intuitive for artists. It later moved toward generative AI, with Masterpiece X, which generates 3D models from text or images. Users describe an object, and the system produces a mesh with textures that can be refined or used as a starting point for game assets, virtual worlds, and prototypes.

The aim is to make output useful in production. Generated models can be downloaded in common formats and used in game engines such as Unity and Unreal, or opened in Blender and other tools for editing. Additional features help with rigging and animation, so characters can be posed and moved without a complex setup. A no-code approach targets creators who do not have a modeling background, including developers and designers who need many assets.

item.title: Mematic
item.description:
Mematic makes meme creation quick on a phone. Users pick a template from a large library or upload their own image, add captions in the classic style, and share to social networks and messaging apps. The interface is built for thumb use, so formatting text is fast.

The app offers sticker and filter options, categories of trending templates, and tools for adding emoji and shapes. A premium subscription removes ads and watermarks and adds more templates and features.

item.title: Meme Generator
item.description:
Meme Generator, at memegenerator.net, lets users pick a template, add top and bottom text, and share the result. Its library includes classic image macros and newer formats, and users can upload their own images. A gallery shows popular memes made with the tool.

The AI features help with captions: a user chooses a template and the tool proposes text, which is useful for getting past the blank caption box. Sharing links and downloads are straightforward.

item.title: Meshcapade
item.description:
Meshcapade grew out of research at the Max Planck Institute on how to represent human bodies in 3D. Its core is SMPL, a parametric model that describes body shape and pose with a small set of numbers, which makes it efficient to generate and animate realistic humans. SMPL has become widely used in computer vision and graphics research, and Meshcapade commercializes the technology.

Its products turn images and video into 3D human data. Motion capture from ordinary video can extract body movement without suits or special cameras, and the output can be used in animation, games, virtual production, and sports analysis. Tools generate avatars with accurate body shapes for virtual try-on in fashion, health and fitness applications, and digital humans. An API lets developers integrate these capabilities, and plugins connect with popular 3D software.

item.title: Microsoft Designer
item.description:
Microsoft Designer helps people make graphics quickly. You describe what you want, such as an invitation for a birthday party or a banner for a sale, and Designer produces several layout options with text, images, and styling, which you can edit. It offers templates for common formats, background removal, and tools for resizing a design for different platforms.

AI image generation is built in, powered by Microsoft’s and OpenAI’s image models, so you can create custom illustrations or photos to include in a design. It integrates with Microsoft 365 apps and Copilot, and is available on the web, as a mobile app, and inside tools such as Edge. Brand kits and shared templates are available on paid Microsoft 365 plans.

item.title: Midjourney
item.description: Midjourney is one of the most popular image generators, valued for its distinctive aesthetic. You describe an image, and it returns variations that tend to look polished and painterly, with strong composition and lighting. It began on Discord, where users type commands in a shared channel, and now offers a web interface with an image editor, personal galleries, and organization tools. It’s widely used by illustrators, designers, concept artists, and marketers.

item.title: Moovly
item.description:
Moovly serves companies that need many versions of the same video. Using a template, teams can generate hundreds or thousands of variations that change names, products, languages, or data, such as personalized sales videos or product videos for each item in a catalog. A browser editor handles design, and an API automates production from spreadsheets or other systems.

Localization is a major theme. Moovly can add subtitles, translate scripts, and generate voiceovers in multiple languages using AI voices, helping companies serve international audiences, and AI tools assist with text-to-video and editing. It’s used in marketing, e-commerce, training, and communications, and offers brand controls and collaboration for large teams.

item.title: Munch
item.description:
Munch focuses on video repurposing. You upload a webinar, podcast, interview, or live stream, or connect a link, and it identifies segments likely to perform well as short clips. Rather than simply cutting at fixed intervals, it analyzes the transcript and content and compares it with trending topics and keywords, then proposes clips with captions, titles, and formatting for TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, and LinkedIn.

Features that support the workflow include automatic captions, reframing to vertical or square, branded templates, and the ability to edit clips before exporting. Social copy and hashtags can be suggested, and a scheduler publishes clips to connected accounts. Marketing teams, agencies, podcasters, and course creators use it to get more from long content without manual editing.

item.title: Murf
item.description: Murf is known for its studio, but its voice features are a separate reason people use it. The voice changer converts a recording of your own speech into a different voice from the library, keeping your timing and emotion, which suits people who want a polished sound without hiring talent. Voice cloning can create a custom voice for a brand or presenter, typically with consent and verification, and is offered mainly for business customers.

item.title: Murf
item.description:
Murf is aimed at people who need a professional voiceover without hiring a voice actor or booking a studio. In its browser-based studio, you paste a script, choose a voice, and adjust pitch, speed, and emphasis. Voices come in many accents and languages and suit narration, e-learning, product videos, ads, and presentations. You can add background music, line the audio up with video or slides, and export the result.

The platform has expanded to related audio jobs. Dubbing translates a video or audio file into other languages and keeps it timed to the original. An API gives developers text-to-speech for their own apps, including fast, streaming voices for conversational use. Murf Agents power voice calls and chat for customer service and similar needs, and a voice changer converts one voice into another. Team workspaces help companies share projects and keep audio consistent.

item.title: Neural.love
item.description:
Neural.love combines creation and repair tools in one web app. The generator creates images from text prompts with a choice of models and styles, while the enhancement tools improve existing pictures. Upscaling increases resolution, denoising cleans grainy photos, and restoration repairs scratches and faded color on old family pictures. Face enhancement can sharpen portraits, and colorization adds color to black-and-white images.

The platform is practical for photographers, genealogists, designers, and anyone with old or low-quality images. Users upload a file, choose the effect, and download the result, with credits consumed by each operation. An API lets developers add enhancement features to their own apps, and batch options handle many images. Generated images can be used in marketing and design, subject to the terms for each plan.

item.title: ON1 Photo AI
item.description:
ON1 Photo AI aims to shorten the path from a raw photo to a finished image. It analyzes a picture and suggests adjustments, then applies tools such as NoNoise AI for removing grain, Sharpener AI for restoring detail, and Super Resolution for enlarging photos. Other tools handle sky replacement, background removal, portrait retouching, and object removal, and automatic masking selects subjects, skies, and other regions for local edits.

It fits into several workflows. It can open and process RAW files directly, work as a standalone app, or run as a plugin inside Lightroom, Photoshop, and other editors, which lets photographers use its AI tools without leaving their usual software. Presets provide quick looks, and batch processing handles many images at once. A separate ON1 Photo RAW product adds organizing and layer-based editing.

item.title: Opus Clip
item.description:
Opus Clip automates a task that eats hours for podcasters, streamers, and marketers: cutting a long recording into shorts. You paste a link or upload a video, and the AI analyzes the transcript and visuals to find segments with a strong hook and a complete idea. It generates several clips, each with a title, captions, and a vertical layout that keeps the speaker in frame.

A virality score estimates how well each clip is likely to perform, based on patterns from social video, which helps you decide what to post first. You can edit the transcript, trim, change caption styles, apply brand templates, and add B-roll. Features such as ClipAnything let you search for a moment by describing it, and a scheduler publishes to connected social accounts.

item.title: Pattern89
item.description:
Pattern89 set out to bring data to creative decisions. Advertisers produce many images and videos but often cannot tell which elements drive results. The platform analyzed an advertiser’s past ads and performance data, tagging the visual and text elements in each, such as colors, faces, products, and calls to action, and learned which combinations worked for a given audience and channel.

With that knowledge, it could score new creative before launch and suggest changes, and recommend which assets to prioritize. Marketers used it to reduce wasted spend on ads that were unlikely to work, and to give designers concrete guidance. Integrations with social ad platforms pulled in performance data.

item.title: Pencil
item.description:
Pencil helps marketing teams produce a steady stream of ads. You connect your brand assets and product information, and Pencil generates video and image ads with copy and voiceovers in different formats for platforms like Meta, TikTok, and YouTube. Teams can create many variations, which makes testing easier than designing each ad by hand.

The prediction layer is the distinctive part. Pencil scores creative on how likely it is to perform, using models trained on a large amount of ad performance data and refined with the account’s own results. It also helps track which messages and visuals win and feeds that back into the next round of creative. Integrations with ad platforms and Shopify bring in performance data and product catalogs.

item.title: Penpot
item.description:
Penpot is built for collaboration between designers and developers. It uses open web standards, so designs map to real code, and supports flexible layouts based on CSS grid and flex. Teams create prototypes, design systems, and shared components in a browser.

Being open source matters to some teams. They can host Penpot themselves, keep control of their data, and avoid vendor lock-in, and developers can inspect designs and get code in a familiar form. AI features and plugins extend the tool.

item.title: Picsart AI
item.description:
Picsart began as a mobile photo editor and grew into a broad creative suite. Users edit photos with filters, collages, stickers, and text, make videos, and design social posts from templates. A community lets people share and remix content, which helped it spread among younger creators and small businesses.

AI is now central. Tools generate images from prompts, remove backgrounds and objects, expand pictures, replace elements, enhance and upscale photos, and create stylized avatars. Text-to-video and animation tools turn ideas into clips, and an AI writer helps with captions. Picsart also provides APIs and plugins so other platforms can use its image tools, and teams can use brand kits and shared workspaces.

item.title: Pictory
item.description:
Pictory is aimed at marketers and content creators who want video without editing skills. You paste a script or a blog URL, and the AI splits the text into scenes, picks stock clips and images for each, adds captions and music, and generates a voiceover. You can then edit scenes, swap visuals, and adjust the text with a simple storyboard-style editor.

Other features extend the same idea. Pictory can summarize a long video, such as a webinar or Zoom recording, into a short highlight reel, create captions, and generate text-to-video clips. A brand kit keeps colors and logos consistent, and integrations let teams pull content from articles. Typical uses are social media videos, explainers, and repurposing blog posts for video platforms.

item.title: Pika Labs
item.description: Pika grew popular by making AI video fun and easy for people with no editing experience. You type a prompt or upload an image, and it generates a short clip in a few moments. Its signature features are effects that change objects in playful ways, such as melting, squishing, inflating, or turning something into cake, which spread quickly across social media. The interface is simple and mobile-friendly, which suited creators who make clips for TikTok and Instagram.

item.title: Pika Labs
item.description:
Pika makes short video easy. A user types a prompt, uploads an image, or provides a clip, and Pika generates or modifies footage. It is known for playful effects, like making objects melt or inflate, as well as realistic motion and camera control.

Creators use it for social posts, ads, and concept work. Features include editing parts of a video, extending clips, adding sound, and lip sync. The platform has expanded to support multiple underlying models and mobile apps.

item.title: Piktochart
item.description: Piktochart is aimed at people who need to present information visually but are not designers. You choose a template for an infographic, report, presentation, or poster, edit the text and images, and add charts and maps that you can link to data. Visual blocks, icons, illustrations, and a library of graphics make it quick to produce clean results, and the tool exports to image and PDF formats or shares online.

item.title: Pixelcut
item.description:
Pixelcut focuses on product images. A seller photographs an item, removes the background in one tap, and places the product on a clean or styled backdrop. AI can generate scenes that suit a product, add shadows, and upscale low-resolution pictures.

Batch tools process many images, and templates help create ads, social posts, and listing graphics. The mobile app is popular with small sellers who shoot products with a phone.

Pixelcut has a free tier and paid plans. AI-generated scenes should still show the product accurately to avoid returns. Alternatives include Photoroom, Canva, Pebblely, Remove.bg, and Adobe Express. Pixelcut suits small online sellers.

item.title: Planner 5D
item.description:
Planner 5D lets anyone design interiors. A user draws walls and rooms, adds furniture from a large catalog, and views the result in 3D from any angle or as a realistic render. It is aimed at homeowners and hobbyists planning remodels, with simple controls.

AI features generate design suggestions from a room photo, restyle spaces, and build floor plans from sketches. A community gallery provides projects to copy and adapt. Mobile and web apps share projects.

item.title: Playground AI
item.description:
Playground started as a place to experiment with image models in a friendly interface. You enter a prompt, choose a model and style, and generate images, then refine them in a canvas that lets you edit parts of a picture, combine elements, and iterate. It was positioned as a flexible tool for artists, designers, and marketers, with a free daily allowance that made it popular for experimentation.

The company has also developed its own image models, which it has promoted for following prompts closely and rendering text, along with tools for creating logos, posters, and social graphics. Image-to-image, upscaling, and editing by instruction help refine results. Users can browse a community feed to see what others are making and borrow ideas.

item.title: Polycam
item.description:
Polycam makes 3D scanning accessible. A user walks around an object or room with their phone, the app captures images or LiDAR depth data, and processing creates a textured 3D model. Models can be measured, shared, and exported for use in design, games, or construction.

Modes include photo-based capture for detail, LiDAR for room scans and floor plans, and tools to build models from photos taken with any camera. Newer features include Gaussian splatting for realistic views and AI tools for generating models from images.

item.title: Powtoon
item.description:
Powtoon helps people make animated videos without an animation background. You start from a template for an explainer, training video, or presentation, edit the text and scenes, and choose characters, props, and backgrounds from a library. A timeline lets you control timing, and you can add voiceovers, music, and screen recordings. It is used for onboarding, corporate communication, education, and marketing.

AI tools reduce the work of getting started. A text-to-video feature creates a draft from a script or topic, AI can write scripts, and text-to-speech generates narration in many languages. Avatars can present, and translation features help localize videos. Branding tools keep colors, fonts, and logos consistent, and collaboration features let teams review and approve content.

item.title: Promethean AI
item.description:
Promethean AI addresses the labor involved in building 3D environments. An artist describes what they want in a scene, such as a cluttered study or a forest clearing, and the assistant selects assets from a library, places them with sensible arrangement and variation, and assembles a draft environment. The aim is to automate repetitive dressing and layout so artists can focus on art direction.

The tool learns from the studio’s own assets and preferences, so output stays consistent with the project’s look, and it integrates with common creative software and engines. It was aimed at game studios, film and virtual production teams, and architectural visualization, where large environments must be filled with believable detail.

item.title: Raw Shorts
item.description:
Raw Shorts aims to make animated explainers accessible to non-designers. You paste a script, an article, or an idea, and the AI breaks it into scenes, chooses animated templates, characters, and icons, and adds a voiceover and music. You can then edit scenes, change visuals, adjust timing, and brand the video with your colors and logo before exporting.

It’s used for marketing explainers, training videos, social clips, and educational content. A library of animated styles, text-to-speech voices in many languages, and options for adding your own media let teams produce a polished video in a short time. Newer features include generating videos from blog posts or presentations.

item.title: Real-ESRGAN
item.description:
Real-ESRGAN takes a small, blurry, or compressed image and produces a larger, cleaner version. It was trained on synthetic damage that imitates real-world degradation, such as blur, noise, and compression artifacts, so it handles messy sources better than older upscalers that assumed clean images. The results often look natural, with sharper edges and textures, although the model adds plausible detail instead of recovering what was truly there.

The project provides several models, including one for general photos and one for anime and illustrations, plus tools for video that process frames. Portable builds run on Windows, macOS, and Linux using Vulkan, so no complicated setup or Nvidia GPU is needed, and Python code lets developers integrate it. It is often paired with GFPGAN for face restoration. Many commercial upscaling tools and apps use Real-ESRGAN or models derived from it.

item.title: Remini
item.description:
Remini gained a following for photo restoration. A user uploads an old family photo or a blurry picture, and the AI sharpens it, repairs damage, and enhances faces. It can also upscale images and colorize black-and-white ones.

The app expanded into AI-generated portraits and avatars from selfies, which went viral at times. Video enhancement is also offered. It runs mainly on phones, with processing in the cloud.

Remini has a free tier with ads and limits, and paid plans, and has faced criticism over subscription practices. Enhancement invents plausible detail, so faces may change from the original. Photos are uploaded, so check the privacy policy. Alternatives include Topaz Photo AI, Let’s Enhance, Photoshop’s neural filters, VanceAI, and Palette.fm. Remini suits people restoring family photos.

item.title: Renderforest
item.description:
Renderforest bundles several creative tools for small businesses. Its video maker offers thousands of templates for intros, explainers, promos, and social videos, with a drag-and-drop editor, stock footage, and music. A logo maker, website builder, and mockup tools round out the suite, so a new business can produce basic branding materials in one place.

AI features speed up creation. Text-to-video tools generate videos from a script or prompt, an AI logo generator proposes designs from a business name, and voiceover and animation helpers add narration and movement. Templates for explainer videos, promos, slideshows, and animated infographics make it quick to produce content for marketing and social media.

item.title: Replica Studios
item.description:
Replica Studios was an Australian startup that made AI voices aimed at creative productions. Its library offered voices of professional actors who had agreed to license their performances, and its tools let game developers and filmmakers generate dialogue with emotion and style. Integrations for game engines such as Unreal and Unity made it easy to put placeholder or final voices into a project, and it also supported voice conversion.

The company drew attention for working with actors instead of against them. It signed an agreement with the actors’ union SAG-AFTRA on terms for licensing digital voice replicas in games, which some actors welcomed and others criticized as inadequate. That debate was part of a wider fight over how AI voices should be used in entertainment, which continues.

item.title: Resemble AI
item.description: Resemble AI builds voices for products and productions. You provide recordings of a speaker, with consent, and the platform trains a voice model that can read any text in that voice, or convert one person’s speech into another voice in real time. Companies use it for branded voices, localization, games, call centers, and media. An API makes it possible to generate speech in applications, and the system supports multiple languages and emotional control.

item.title: Rive
item.description: Rive aims to make animation behave like part of an app. In its editor, designers draw vector shapes, rig them with bones, and animate them on a timeline. The key difference from video or GIF is the state machine: animations can have states and transitions that react to inputs, such as a button being pressed, a character getting closer, or a progress value changing. This lets one asset handle many behaviors.

item.title: Runway
item.description:
Runway builds tools for creative professionals. Its generative video models create clips from text or images, and a suite of editing tools handles tasks like removing backgrounds, changing motion, extending shots, and applying styles. Everything runs in the browser.

The company began with accessible video editing and became a leader in generative video, working with artists and studios. Newer models offer longer clips, better consistency, and controls for camera and motion, and the platform includes workflows for combining generation with traditional editing.

item.title: Runway
item.description: Runway is one of the original AI video companies, and it built its tools with filmmakers and artists in mind. The core of the product is its Gen video models, which create short clips from a text prompt, a still image, or both. Reference images help keep a character or setting consistent from one shot to the next, which is the hard part of making anything longer than a single clip. The company started as a set of browser-based editing tools, and some of that remains, such as background removal, motion tracking, and inpainting.

item.title: Runway Gen-3
item.description:
Gen-3 Alpha improved on earlier versions with finer detail, better handling of motion, and more consistent results across frames. Users could generate clips of several seconds from a prompt, an image, or both, with controls for camera movement and style.

It was trained on both images and video, aiming to understand how things move, and supported features such as image-to-video and video-to-video. Filmmakers and agencies used it for concept work, ads, and visual effects experiments.

item.title: Scenario
item.description:
Scenario is built around consistency, which is the main challenge of using generative AI in game production. A studio uploads examples of its art, and Scenario trains a custom model that learns the style, so the characters, props, and environments it generates look like they belong in the same game. Artists can use it to create concepts, variations, and finished assets faster.

The platform covers more than still images. It can generate sprites, textures, icons, and UI elements, create variations of existing pieces, convert images into 3D models, and offers workflows for upscaling and cleaning outputs. An API and plugins connect it to game engines and pipelines, and team features support collaboration and asset management. The focus is on production use by studios and indie developers.

item.title: SeaArt
item.description: SeaArt gives users a rich set of image generation tools in a friendly interface. You write a prompt, choose among many models and styles, and generate images, with options such as ControlNet to guide pose or composition and LoRA models to apply particular styles or characters. A library of community-shared models, workflows, and characters lets users build on others’ work, and a node-based workflow editor offers more advanced control for those who want it.

item.title: simpleshow
item.description:
simpleshow is known for its hand-drawn, paper-cutout explainer style. A user pastes a script or topic, and the engine suggests images and structure, generates a video with narration, and lets the user edit scenes. The goal is to make complex subjects clear for training and communications.

Companies use it for onboarding, compliance, product explanations, and internal updates. The platform is aimed at non-designers and provides templates and a library of illustrations.

item.title: Sketch
item.description:
Sketch helped define modern interface design. Designers create screens with vectors and reusable symbols, build design systems, and prototype interactions. Its Mac-native app is fast and has a large plugin ecosystem.

Collaboration moved to the web, where teammates view, comment, and hand off designs, and a Windows-compatible web editor extends access. AI features help generate placeholder content, adjust layouts, and speed up repetitive work.

Sketch is sold by subscription. Figma has taken much of its market because of browser-based collaboration. Alternatives include Figma, Penpot, Adobe XD (no longer developed), Framer, and Affinity Designer. Sketch suits Mac-based designers who prefer a native tool.

item.title: SketchUp
item.description: SketchUp is known for being easy to learn. Its core idea is pushing and pulling flat shapes into 3D forms, which makes it quick to sketch a building, a room, or a piece of furniture. Architects use it for early design, interior designers for layouts, and construction and woodworking professionals for planning and shop drawings. The 3D Warehouse offers a huge library of free models of furniture, fixtures, and building components.

item.title: Smartly.io
item.description:
Smartly, formerly Smartly.io, serves brands and agencies that run large ad programs. Its platform connects to major social networks and lets teams build and launch many campaigns from one interface, apply rules, and update thousands of ads at once. For retailers with big catalogs, dynamic ads are generated automatically from product feeds, adjusting to inventory and price.

The product emphasizes creative and optimization. Creative automation produces many ad variations in different sizes and languages from templates, which helps with testing and localization. Predictive budget allocation shifts spend among campaigns based on performance, and reporting brings results across platforms together. Newer generative features help create and adapt creative assets, with brand controls.

item.title: Speechify
item.description: Speechify turns reading into listening. You import text from the web, a PDF, an email, or a photo of a page, and the app reads it aloud at the speed you choose, highlighting the words as it goes. That makes it useful for catching up on articles while commuting, for studying, and for people with dyslexia or other reading differences, who often find audio easier to process. Apps for iOS, Android, Chrome, and the web sync your library.

item.title: Spline
item.description:
Spline brings 3D to web designers. In a browser editor that feels more like Figma than Blender, you create shapes, materials, lighting, and animations, then add interactions such as hover effects and clicks. Scenes can be published as links, embedded in websites, or exported to code, and they run in real time in the browser. It’s used for product landing pages, interactive hero sections, games, and design prototypes.

Collaboration and AI features set it apart from traditional 3D tools. Multiple people can edit a scene at once with comments and version history. AI tools can generate 3D objects and textures from text, help with animation, and create scenes from prompts. Physics, particles, and state-based interactions add depth, and integrations with Figma let designers bring in 2D elements.

item.title: Stable Video Diffusion
item.description:
Stable Video Diffusion extends the Stable Diffusion approach to motion. A user supplies a still image, and the model generates a few seconds of video that animates the scene. It was released with open weights, so researchers and hobbyists could run and adapt it.

Many later tools and workflows built on it, adding controls, longer clips, and fine-tunes. It helped prove that open video models were feasible, though newer models from other labs have surpassed it in length and quality.

item.title: StarryAI
item.description:
StarryAI brought AI art generation to phones. In the app, you enter a text prompt, pick an art style or model, and receive images within a minute or so. Styles range from fantasy and anime to realism and abstract, and you can use an image as a starting point for variations. It’s aimed at hobbyists and creators who want art for wallpapers, profile pictures, book covers, or game concepts.

Features support experimentation. You can control aspect ratio, choose among models, and upscale results, and a gallery shows creations from other users for inspiration. Different pricing tiers offer more credits and faster generation, and the terms for commercial use vary by plan, with ownership of outputs depending on the subscription.

item.title: Steve AI
item.description:
Steve AI is a text-to-video tool aimed at people who need videos without filming. You paste a script, an article, or a prompt, and the platform creates a video with scenes, characters or stock footage, text, voiceover, and music, which you can edit. It offers animated styles and live-action style videos built from stock clips.

It supports many typical use cases. Marketers create explainers and promos, educators make lesson videos, and social media managers turn blog posts into short clips. Options include different aspect ratios, branding, and a library of characters and backgrounds. Voiceover and avatar features add narration in various languages.

item.title: StockImg AI
item.description:
StockImg AI turns a description into a usable image. Instead of searching a stock library for something close to what you imagine, you type what you want and the tool creates it. It offers separate generators geared to common needs: logo designs, ebook and book covers, posters, wallpapers, illustrations, and app screen mockups. Each has settings suited to its format, such as aspect ratios for covers and posters.

The tool also includes editing functions. You can adjust and regenerate images, remove backgrounds, and explore variations. Self-publishers, small businesses, bloggers, and social media managers use it to get covers and graphics without hiring a designer or paying for licenses. The output is meant to be unique to your prompt, which avoids the problem of the same stock photo showing up in many places.

item.title: Synthesia
item.description:
Synthesia produces videos with digital presenters. Users select from a library of avatars or create a custom one, paste a script, choose a voice and language, and receive a finished video. The editor handles slides, text, and media.

Companies use it for training, onboarding, product explainers, and communications, often replacing costly shoots. Translations let one video serve many markets. Recent features add interactive videos, screen recording, and avatars with more expressive delivery.

item.title: Synthesia
item.description:
Synthesia lets companies produce videos without cameras, studios, or actors. A user writes or pastes a script, selects an AI avatar from a library of presenters or creates a custom one, and the platform generates a video with natural speech and lip movement. Scenes, slides, screen recordings, and media can be combined, and editing the script and regenerating takes the place of a reshoot.

The platform is built for business use. It supports a large number of languages, so one video can be localized quickly, and offers templates, brand kits, and collaboration features. Interactive and agent-style avatars can respond to viewers, and an API lets teams automate video creation. Enterprise features cover security, compliance, and consent controls, since custom avatars require permission from the person depicted. Companies commonly use it for learning and development, onboarding, product explainers, and sales content.

item.title: Topaz Photo AI
item.description:
Topaz Photo AI aims to fix the technical flaws in photos with little effort. When you open an image, it analyzes the content and suggests corrections, using models for noise reduction, sharpening, and increasing resolution. It handles problems like grainy high-ISO shots, soft focus, and motion blur, and can enlarge photos while adding believable detail. Many wildlife, sports, and event photographers use it to rescue difficult images.

The tool also offers face recovery, light adjustment, color balance, and a way to apply different adjustments to selected subjects. It can be run as a standalone application, as an external editor from Lightroom, or as a plugin for Photoshop, and processes batches of images. Models run locally on your computer and benefit from a good graphics card.

item.title: Topaz Video AI
item.description:
Topaz Video AI improves footage after it has been shot. Its models upscale low-resolution video to HD or 4K, remove noise and compression artifacts, and sharpen soft footage. Frame interpolation creates additional frames to make slow motion smoother or convert a low frame rate to a higher one, and stabilization steadies shaky shots. Archivists restoring old film and videographers rescuing difficult footage use it often.

Different models are tuned for different problems, such as live action, animation, or low-quality sources. Newer diffusion-based models aim for higher-quality enhancement of detail, at the cost of heavy processing. The app lets you preview results on short clips before processing a whole video, supports batch processing and command-line use, and exports to common formats, with some cloud options for heavy models.

item.title: Upscayl
item.description: Upscayl makes AI upscaling available to anyone. You drag in a low-resolution image, choose a model, and the app enlarges it by two, three, or four times with added detail, saving the result to your computer. It includes models tuned for general photos, digital art, and sharpening, and supports batch processing for many files. Because it runs on your own hardware, there is no per-image fee, and your images stay private.

item.title: Vectorizer.ai
item.description:
Vectorizer.ai converts bitmap images into vectors, which are scalable files used for logos, print, and cutting machines. Upload a low-resolution logo or illustration, and the service traces the shapes into paths and fills, returning an SVG, EPS, PDF, or DXF that can be resized without losing sharpness. The AI approach produces cleaner curves and fewer stray points than older tracing tools, with controls to adjust the level of detail.

Designers use it to recover logos from low-quality files, sign makers and crafters use it to prepare artwork for vinyl cutters and laser engravers, and developers add it to workflows through an API. It handles flat-color artwork best, such as logos and icons, and it works less well on photographs, which turn into complex tracings with many shapes. A preview lets you see the result before paying.

item.title: VEED.io
item.description:
VEED is an online video editor that makes common edits simple. You upload clips, trim and arrange them on a timeline, add text, music, and effects, and export in formats for different platforms. It includes a screen and webcam recorder for tutorials and messages, templates for social videos, and stock media. Everything runs in the browser, which allows collaboration without installing software.

AI features are a big part of the draw. Auto subtitles transcribe and style captions in many languages, background removal and noise cleanup polish footage, eye contact correction makes you appear to look at the camera, and AI avatars and voices generate presenter videos from scripts. Tools for translation and dubbing help reach other markets, and an assistant can clean up speech by removing filler words and silences.

item.title: Venngage
item.description:
Venngage targets people who need to communicate information visually. Users start from thousands of templates for infographics, reports, flyers, presentations, and social graphics, replace the content, and customize colors, icons, and charts. Data can be imported to generate charts, and the tool includes maps and diagrams for explaining processes and comparisons.

It differentiates itself with business features. Brand kits apply logos, fonts, and colors automatically, team workspaces allow collaboration and approvals, and an accessibility checker flags color contrast and other issues. AI tools generate infographic designs from text, write copy, and suggest improvements, and designs can be exported or shared with analytics.

item.title: Vidyo.ai
item.description:
Vidyo.ai set out to save creators the time of cutting short clips from podcasts, webinars, and long videos. You upload a video or paste a link, and the AI analyzes the content to find segments that could stand alone, then produces clips with captions and a vertical layout. You can edit the transcript, adjust the clip boundaries, and customize caption styles before exporting.

The company has rebranded to quso.ai, expanding from a clipping tool into a broader social content platform. It now includes features for scheduling posts across social networks, analytics on performance, and AI helpers for creating captions and ideas. Accounts and plans carried over from Vidyo.ai, and the core clipping features continue.

item.title: Visily
item.description:
Visily is built for people who need to mock up interfaces quickly without learning a full design tool. You can upload a screenshot of an app, a hand-drawn sketch, or a description of a screen, and the AI creates an editable wireframe made of real components. A library of templates, UI kits, and smart components helps assemble screens for web and mobile products.

Collaboration is part of the appeal. Teams can edit together, leave comments, and share clickable prototypes with stakeholders, and designs can be exported or moved into Figma for refinement.
