Product managers, business analysts, and founders use it to communicate ideas visually and gather feedback early, before engineering work starts.

item.title: Voicemod
item.description: Voicemod changes how you sound as you speak. You choose a voice effect, such as a robot, a deep voice, or a character, and the app processes your microphone audio in real time. It works as a virtual microphone, so apps like Discord, Zoom, OBS, and many games treat it like a normal mic. Gamers and streamers use it for fun and for roleplay, and some people use it for privacy.

item.title: Vyond
item.description:
Vyond focuses on business animation. Users build videos from libraries of characters, props, and backgrounds, choosing actions and expressions for each character and arranging scenes on a timeline. The style is a recognizable cartoon format popular in corporate training, compliance courses, and explainer videos, and the tool makes it possible to produce them without animation skills.

AI features reduce the work of getting started. A text-to-video capability generates a draft video from a script or prompt, including scenes, characters, and voiceover, which you can then edit. Other tools produce voices in many languages, help with translations, and match lip sync. Branded templates and shared libraries help teams keep their videos consistent, and enterprise features cover security and administration.

item.title: Waifu2x
item.description: Waifu2x was one of the first widely used AI image upscalers. Created for anime and illustration, it uses convolutional neural networks to double the size of an image while reducing noise and compression artifacts. A free web demo made it easy to try, and downloadable versions let people run it locally, including ports that work on many graphics cards through Vulkan. It became a standard tool for enlarging fan art, wallpapers, and screenshots.

item.title: Wave.video
item.description:
Wave.video bundles several tools that marketers often use separately. The editor handles videos from templates, with stock footage, music, and text animations for social posts, ads, and promos. A recorder captures your screen or webcam, a live streaming studio broadcasts to multiple platforms, and a hosting service stores and embeds videos with customizable players and calls to action.

AI features help produce videos faster. Tools convert text or a blog post into a video draft, generate captions and subtitles, resize videos for different social formats, and create voiceovers. Brand kits keep colors and logos consistent, and integrations link with email platforms and social networks. It’s targeted at small businesses, agencies, and content teams.

item.title: Whimsical AI
item.description:
Whimsical puts several lightweight visual tools in one place. You can draw flowcharts and sequence diagrams, sketch low-fidelity wireframes, brainstorm on mind maps, write docs, and arrange sticky notes on a board. The tools are designed around speed, with keyboard shortcuts, snapping, and a clean look that makes rough thinking easy to share.

AI features reduce the setup. Describe a process and Whimsical can draft a flowchart, turn a topic into a mind map, or produce a first-pass wireframe, which you then edit by hand. Teams use it for planning, product specs, and explaining systems, and sharing is simple with links, comments, and embeds in tools like Notion and Confluence.

item.title: ACE Studio
item.description: ACE Studio lets musicians create vocals without a singer. You enter a melody in a piano-roll editor along with lyrics, choose a voice model, and the software sings it, with controls for vibrato, breath, dynamics, and expression that make the performance sound human. It works as a standalone app or as a plugin inside digital audio workstations such as Ableton, Logic, and FL Studio. Songwriters use it for demos and finished tracks.

item.title: Alpha3D
item.description: Alpha3D addresses a bottleneck in 3D content: modeling each object by hand is slow and expensive. Instead, you upload a photo of a product or describe an object in text, and the platform generates a 3D model, typically within minutes. The models can be downloaded in common formats such as GLB for use in game engines, web viewers, and AR experiences. The company positions it for retail, gaming, and virtual try-on.

item.title: Animoto
item.description:
Animoto was built for people who need a video quickly and do not know editing software. A user uploads photos and video clips, picks a template and a song, and the tool arranges them into a polished video with text and transitions. A storyboard view lets you rearrange scenes and change styles.

It aims at small businesses, real estate agents, educators, and social media marketers. Templates fit common formats such as promos, slideshows, and testimonials, and brand tools apply logos and colors. Videos can be shared online or exported for ads and websites. Newer AI features speed up layout and text creation.

item.title: Convai
item.description:
Convai makes game characters that respond to what players say. A developer defines a character’s personality, backstory, and knowledge, and Convai handles listening to speech, generating replies with a language model, speaking them with a synthetic voice, and driving lip sync and gestures. Plugins integrate with Unity, Unreal Engine, and other platforms.

Characters can also take actions in the game world, such as navigating or interacting with objects, based on conversation. Use cases include immersive games, training simulations, virtual tours, and educational experiences where open-ended dialogue adds value over scripted lines.

item.title: CSM AI
item.description:
CSM turns simple inputs into 3D assets. A user uploads a picture, types a description, or draws a sketch, and the system produces a 3D model with textures that can be exported to common formats. It supports game developers, designers, and creators who need assets quickly.

Beyond single objects, it offers tools for character creation and animation preparation, and an API lets developers build 3D generation into their own apps. The output is often a starting point that artists clean up, since generated meshes can have topology problems that matter for animation and games.

item.title: Hedra
item.description:
Hedra animates faces. A user supplies a still image, which can be a photo, illustration, or generated character, and an audio track or script, and Hedra produces a video of the character speaking with matching lip movement and expression. The results are known for emotive performances.

Uses include short films, explainer videos, social content with characters, and marketing. Text to speech and voice options make it possible to start from only a script, and longer and higher resolution outputs are available on paid plans. The platform has expanded into broader video generation features.

item.title: Jammable
item.description:
Jammable, formerly Voicify, lets people hear songs sung in a different voice. A user chooses a voice model from a library, uploads a vocal or song, and the system converts it so it sounds like the chosen voice. Fans and creators use it for parodies, mashups, and experiments.

The technology raises serious legal and ethical issues. Voices of real artists are protected in many places, and music labels and artists have objected to unauthorized voice clones. Sharing such covers can violate copyright and rights of publicity, and platforms may remove them. Use voices you have permission to use, and avoid presenting synthetic songs as the real artist.

item.title: Kaiber
item.description:
Kaiber is known for stylized, artistic video. A user supplies a prompt, an image, or a video clip, chooses a style, and the platform generates moving footage in that look. Audio reactivity lets visuals respond to a music track, which made it a favorite for music videos and live visuals.

The platform has grown into a broader creative studio with a canvas for combining generated images and video and with access to several underlying models. Artists use it to experiment with motion and aesthetics rather than realistic footage, and it has been featured in music video projects.

item.title: Kits AI
item.description:
Kits AI targets music creators. A producer can record a vocal and convert it into another singer’s voice from a library, create a model of their own voice for consistent takes, or separate a song into vocals and instruments to remix. A text to speech option and tools for vocal cleanup are included.

Its distinguishing approach is licensing. Kits offers voices from artists who have agreed to participate and be paid, which contrasts with unauthorized voice clones that raise copyright and rights-of-publicity problems. Users still need to follow license terms for how converted vocals are released.

item.title: Klap
item.description:
Klap helps creators and marketers turn long videos into shorts. A user uploads a video or pastes a link, and the tool picks promising segments, crops them to vertical format while tracking the speaker, and adds captions. A score estimates how likely each clip is to perform.

The clips can be edited to adjust timing, captions, and layout, and published or exported. Podcasters, coaches, webinar hosts, and YouTubers use it to get more mileage from content they already have. Language support lets clips be captioned or dubbed for other audiences.

item.title: Latitude
item.description:
Latitude makes interactive fiction with AI. Its best-known product, AI Dungeon, lets players describe any action in natural language, and an AI game master responds with the next part of the story. The result is open-ended storytelling that can go in any direction, from fantasy quests to comedy and mystery.

The studio has experimented with other AI-driven games and with platforms for creators who want to build their own AI-powered worlds. It uses a mix of language models, including models it trains and fine-tunes, and offers different tiers of models to subscribers.

item.title: Lexica
item.description:
Lexica began as a searchable archive of AI-generated images with the prompts that created them. Browsing the archive helped people learn how wording affects results, and copy ideas for their own generations. That made it a popular learning resource in the early days of image generators.

The platform added its own image generation models and an editor, so users can create images, refine them, and organize collections. It offers different model options and tools for art, product shots, and concepts. The community library remains a source of inspiration.

item.title: Lummi
item.description:
Lummi collects AI-generated pictures in a searchable library, organized by category and style. Users browse or search for backgrounds, textures, scenes, and illustrations, then download them for use in websites, presentations, and campaigns. The pitch is variety and a modern look compared with familiar stock photography.

The platform includes generation tools that let users create images from prompts and adjust them, along with options for editing. It is popular with designers who want unusual or abstract visuals and do not want to prompt from scratch.

item.title: Madgicx
item.description:
Madgicx is built for performance marketers and e-commerce brands running paid social. It connects to ad accounts and analyzes campaigns, then recommends or applies changes such as shifting budget toward better-performing ad sets, pausing losers, or testing new audiences. Automation rules run these changes continuously.

Creative tools help with the content side. The platform analyzes which creatives perform best and helps generate variations, and reporting dashboards combine data from ads and online stores into one view. Audience tools find lookalike segments and retargeting groups.

item.title: Magnific AI
item.description:
Magnific AI takes a low-resolution image and produces a larger version with added, invented detail. Users control how much creative freedom the AI takes with settings such as creativity and resemblance, and can add a prompt describing what the detail should look like. This makes it different from conventional upscalers.

Artists use it to polish AI-generated images and to turn rough concept art into detailed illustrations. Designers use it to prepare images for large formats. The company was acquired by Freepik, and the technology is available through Magnific’s own site and Freepik’s tools.

item.title: Moises
item.description:
Moises helps musicians work with recordings. A user uploads a song, and the app splits it into individual tracks, so a guitarist can mute the guitar and play along, or a singer can remove the lead vocal for practice. Tempo and key changes help with learning difficult parts.

Extra tools include chord detection, a metronome, and a feature to detect beats. Producers use stem separation for remixes and sampling, and teachers use it to demonstrate parts. Mobile and web apps make it easy to practice anywhere.

item.title: Morph Studio
item.description:
Morph Studio lets users create video through prompts and images. It offers a storyboard interface, where a creator plans shots, generates each, and assembles them into a sequence, which suits narrative content more than single clips. Different models and styles are available.

Creators use it for short films, ads, music videos, and social content. The workflow supports iteration: regenerate a shot, adjust the prompt, and compare results. Community features let users share work and learn techniques.

item.title: Musicfy
item.description:
Musicfy offers several music tools in one place. Users can generate a track from a text prompt, convert one instrument or vocal to another voice or sound, separate a song into stems, and create voice covers with AI voices. It is aimed at creators who want to experiment with songs without a studio.

The same tools raise rights questions. Copying a real artist’s voice without permission can violate publicity and copyright rules, and platforms and labels remove such content. Generated music has varying licensing terms, so read them before releasing or monetizing songs.

item.title: PixAI
item.description:
PixAI is built around anime-style generation. Users type prompts, pick models trained for particular looks, and generate images. A feed of community creations offers inspiration, and sharing prompts lets others learn techniques.

Features include image-to-image transformation, model and LoRA libraries, and tools for creating characters consistently. A mobile app and credit system support casual use.

PixAI has a free tier with daily credits and paid plans. Community models can be trained on artwork without artists’ consent, which is controversial, and content rules apply to the platform. Alternatives include Civitai, Leonardo AI, NovelAI, Midjourney with niji, and Tensor.Art. PixAI suits anime fans and illustrators exploring AI art.

item.title: Recraft
item.description:
Recraft is aimed at designers. Besides raster images, it can produce true vector graphics, such as logos, icons, and illustrations, that remain sharp at any size and can be edited in design software. Style controls keep outputs consistent across a project.

Brand features let a team upload colors, fonts, and example images so generations follow a style. The model handles text in images well, which helps with posters and mockups. Editing tools allow changing parts of an image, removing backgrounds, and upscaling.

item.title: Respeecher
item.description:
Respeecher works through speech-to-speech conversion. A performer records a line, and the system transforms it into the voice of a target speaker, keeping the performer’s emotion and timing. This differs from text-to-speech, which generates speech from scratch and can lack nuance.

Productions have used it to recreate the voices of actors who are unavailable, age or de-age a voice, and dub into other languages while preserving a character’s sound. The company emphasizes licensing and consent from voice owners.

item.title: Riffusion
item.description:
Riffusion started as a research demo that generated music clips by running Stable Diffusion on spectrogram images, an early sign that diffusion models could make audio. It grew into a platform where users type a prompt and get a song with vocals, and into a chat-like agent that helps produce tracks.

The brand changed to Producer.ai, and reports say it has since moved under Google’s music efforts, so product names and features may keep changing. Users should check the current site and how their saved songs and rights are handled through any transition.

item.title: Rodin
item.description:
Rodin creates 3D assets from simple inputs. A user types a description or uploads an image, and the system produces a textured 3D model that can be exported to common formats. It also offers options for controlling geometry and materials.

The output can serve as a starting point for games, animation, product visualization, and augmented reality. Quality has improved quickly in this field, but generated meshes often need cleanup of topology and textures before production use.

item.title: RoomGPT
item.description:
RoomGPT lets people visualize a space in new styles. A user uploads a photo of a living room or bedroom, chooses a theme such as modern, minimalist, or tropical, and the AI generates redesigned images that keep the room’s structure while changing furniture and decor.

Homeowners use it for inspiration before shopping or renovating, and some real estate agents use it for staging ideas. Results show style direction but do not match real products or exact dimensions.

item.title: Sloyd
item.description:
Sloyd takes a different approach from mesh generators. Its models are parametric, so a user can generate a chair or a sword and then adjust sliders for size, shape, and style, and get clean, game-ready geometry with proper topology. Real-time generation fits into workflows and game engines.

A library of templates and an API let developers generate assets inside their own tools and games, including at runtime. The aim is to reduce the time artists spend on common props and set dressing.

item.title: Splice
item.description:
Splice supplies the building blocks of modern production. Producers search a huge catalog of samples by genre, key, and tempo, preview them in sync with their project, and download them under a license that allows use in released music. Plugin subscriptions let users rent instruments and effects.

AI features assist with creativity. Tools suggest compatible samples, and apps generate loops and ideas. Cloud project backup and collaboration features help producers work with others.

item.title: Stable Audio
item.description:
Stable Audio generates sound from descriptions. A user types a prompt such as an upbeat electronic track with a driving bass line, and the model produces a piece of the requested length. It can also create sound effects and ambient textures.

The models were trained on licensed audio, which Stability emphasizes to address rights concerns. Producers and sound designers use it for sketching ideas, backing tracks, and game audio. Smaller open models can run locally.

item.title: Stablecog
item.description:
Stablecog offers image generation without the setup of running a model locally. Users enter a prompt, choose a model and settings, and receive images in seconds. The code is open, and the project is run as a community-minded service.

It appeals to hobbyists who want to try Stable Diffusion and its variants and to developers who want a reference for building their own interface. Free credits are available, with paid options for more use.

item.title: Tailor Brands
item.description:
Tailor Brands serves new businesses. A user enters a company name and preferences, and the AI proposes logos and a brand kit with colors and fonts, then applies it to business cards, social graphics, and a website. The goal is a complete starter identity in minutes.

The platform has added services around the brand: website building, domain, and incorporation help. Subscriptions bundle logos and tools.

Tailor Brands has a free tier to design and paid plans to download. AI logos can resemble others, and trademark checks are the user’s job. Alternatives include Looka, Canva, LogoAI, Wix Logo Maker, and hiring a designer. Tailor Brands suits small business owners starting a brand.

item.title: Tensor.Art
item.description:
Tensor.Art lets people create images without owning a GPU. They choose from a library of models and LoRAs trained by the community, type a prompt, and generate images, often in styles from anime to realism. Workflows can be remixed, and results shared in a gallery.

The platform supports training custom models, running ComfyUI-based workflows, and generating video, and it has a credit system for heavy use. It appeals to hobbyists and artists who want variety.

item.title: Unakin
item.description:
Unakin targets game studios. Its agents take requests in natural language and help create parts of a game, such as environments, items, interfaces, and gameplay logic, and assist with finding and fixing bugs. The pitch is a smaller team doing more in less time.

Prototyping is a main use, letting designers test ideas before investing heavily. Code assistance for Unity helps developers learn unfamiliar parts of a project.

Independent information is limited, so confirm current availability and pricing on the company’s site. Game development has quality and licensing concerns about AI-generated assets. Alternatives include Unity’s AI tools, Scenario, Inworld, Convai, and general coding assistants like Cursor. Unakin suits game teams exploring AI helpers.

item.title: Vidnoz
item.description:
Vidnoz offers avatar-based video. A user picks from a library of presenters, pastes a script, selects a voice and language, and generates a clip. A template library, a video editor, and tools such as face swap and voice cloning broaden the toolkit.

Marketers use it for explainers and ads, and educators for lessons. A free tier lets users try it, with limits on minutes and watermarks.

Vidnoz has a free plan and paid tiers. Features like face swap and voice cloning carry consent and misuse concerns. Alternatives include Synthesia, HeyGen, Elai.io, D-ID, and Hour One. Vidnoz suits budget-conscious users making avatar videos.

item.title: Vidu
item.description:
Vidu turns prompts into short videos. A user writes a description or supplies reference images, and the platform generates a clip. Features include reference-to-video, which keeps a character or object consistent across shots, and templates for effects that are popular in social content.

The company is one of several Chinese labs competing in video generation, alongside Kling, MiniMax, and others, and its models have gained attention for motion quality and speed. Creators use it for short films, ads, and animation tests.

item.title: Vizard
item.description:
Vizard helps creators repurpose long content. A user uploads a podcast, webinar, or interview, and the tool analyzes it to pick highlight moments, cuts them into clips, crops them for vertical formats, and adds captions. A text-based editor lets users trim by editing the transcript.

Extra features include B-roll suggestions, brand templates, and scheduling to social platforms. It supports many languages and serves podcasters, educators, and marketers.

Vizard has a free tier and paid plans by minutes. Clip selection is automated and may not match a creator’s taste, so review matters. Alternatives include OpusClip, Klap, Submagic, Descript, and Munch. Vizard suits creators making short clips from long recordings.

item.title: Wisecut
item.description:
Wisecut speeds up editing of simple videos. A creator uploads a recording, and the tool detects pauses and filler, cuts them, adds smooth transitions, and generates subtitles from the transcript. Background music automatically ducks when someone speaks.

It helps podcasters, educators, and social creators who want clean videos without learning a full editor. Autoreframe adapts videos to different aspect ratios, and the transcript lets users edit by text.

Wisecut has a free tier and paid plans. It handles basic edits, so complex projects need a fuller editor. Alternatives include Descript, CapCut, Submagic, Kapwing, and VEED. Wisecut suits creators editing talking-head content.

item.title: Adobe Express
item.description:
Adobe Express is Adobe’s answer to Canva: a simple editor where you start from a template, change the text and images, and export. It covers social media posts, banners, flyers, simple videos, and quick edits to PDFs. It runs in the browser and on phones, and it needs no design background. Brand kits, shared templates, and a content scheduler help small teams keep their posts consistent.

The AI tools come from Adobe’s Firefly models. You can generate images from a text prompt, extend or fill parts of a photo, apply text effects from a description, remove backgrounds, and resize a design for several platforms in one step. Because it shares libraries with Creative Cloud, assets from Photoshop or Illustrator can be used directly in Express projects, and designers can hand off a template that colleagues then adjust.

item.title: Aiter.io
item.description:
Aiter.io aims at the problem of generic AI marketing copy. A user enters a website address, and the tool reads the site to understand the product, audience, and tone. It then drafts ad variations, social posts, and email campaigns that follow that voice, so small teams can produce material without starting from a blank page.

This kind of tool is meant for founders and small marketing teams who lack time or staff. It can produce a first set of campaign assets quickly, which a person then edits and approves. Output quality depends heavily on how clear the website is, and any generated claim needs checking for accuracy.

item.title: BestPhotoAI
item.description:
BestPhotoAI is meant for fast photo improvement. A user uploads an image, and the tool can sharpen details, increase resolution, fix lighting and color, and retouch skin, then returns an enhanced version. The aim is to save time compared with manual editing in Photoshop or Lightroom.

Typical users are e-commerce sellers who need clean product photos, creators preparing profile and social images, and people restoring older pictures. Automated enhancement works best on ordinary issues like low light or noise, and results vary with the source image.

item.title: Bing Image Creator
item.description: Bing Image Creator made AI image generation easy to try. You type a description, and it returns several images within a few seconds, with no installation and no cost beyond a Microsoft account. Its popularity came from being free and being available inside Bing and Edge, long before many alternatives had a free tier. Microsoft has since renamed the tool Image Creator from Designer and tied it into Copilot and the Designer app.

item.title: CapCut
item.description:
CapCut became popular for short-form video because it is easy to use and well connected to TikTok. You can assemble clips on a timeline, trim and cut, add music and transitions, and apply effects, filters, and animated text. Templates let you drop your footage into a ready-made edit, which is a quick route to a polished social video. It runs on iOS, Android, Windows, macOS, and in the browser.

The AI features are a major draw. Auto captions transcribe speech and style subtitles, background removal works without a green screen, and smart tools stabilize footage, retouch faces, and clean up audio. Newer capabilities include AI avatars, voice changing and text-to-speech, translation, image and video generation, and tools that cut long videos into short clips. Together they speed up work for creators who post often.

item.title: ClipDrop
item.description:
Clipdrop packages common image edits into simple web tools. Remove Background cuts out a subject in a click, Cleanup erases unwanted objects, Image Upscaler enlarges small pictures with added detail, and Uncrop extends an image beyond its borders. Relight changes the lighting on a subject, and Replace Background swaps in a new scene from a text prompt. A text-to-image generator rounds out the set, using Stability AI models.

Product photographers, e-commerce sellers, marketers, and casual users reach for it when they need a quick edit without opening a heavy editor. The tools work in the browser and on mobile, with an API for developers who want to add the same features to their own apps. The project had a short stint under Stability AI before moving to Jasper, which acquired it to expand its marketing tools.

item.title: ClipFinder
item.description:
ClipFinder helps creators repurpose long content. A streamer or podcaster uploads or links a long recording, and the tool analyzes it for moments that stand out, such as reactions, jokes, or key points, then cuts them into short clips. This saves hours that would otherwise go to scrubbing through footage.

The clips can be formatted for vertical platforms such as TikTok, YouTube Shorts, and Instagram Reels, often with captions. Creators review the suggestions, trim as needed, and publish. The tool is aimed at those who produce hours of material and lack an editor.

item.title: DALL-E 3
item.description:
DALL-E 3 was a text-to-image model known for following detailed prompts closely. Its integration with ChatGPT let users describe an image in conversation and have the assistant refine the prompt, which made image generation accessible to people who had never used a dedicated art tool. Developers could also call it through OpenAI’s API.

It was part of a line that began with the original DALL-E and DALL-E 2, which helped popularize text-to-image generation. Over time, OpenAI moved to newer image models built natively into its multimodal systems, which handle text in images and edits better. DALL-E branding faded as a result.

item.title: EchoWrite
item.description:
EchoWrite aims to make dictation work everywhere on a Windows PC. A user presses a hotkey, speaks, and the text appears in the active application, such as a word processor, email client, or code editor. AI cleans up punctuation and filler words so the result reads closer to written text.

Voice typing is faster than typing for many people, and helps those with repetitive strain issues. Accuracy depends on the microphone, accent, and vocabulary, and a quiet environment helps. Specialized terms may need custom dictionaries.

item.title: Erase.bg
item.description:
Erase.bg handles one of the most common editing jobs. You upload a picture of a product, person, or object, and an AI model detects the foreground and removes the background, producing a PNG with transparency. It works on people, products, animals, and cars, and handles complex edges like hair reasonably well. Typical users are online sellers, designers, and anyone making a profile picture or a presentation.

Several features make it more practical for volume work. Batch processing lets you upload many images at once, and an API and plugins integrate with design tools and workflows. After removing the background, you can add a solid color, a new image, or leave it transparent. A free tier gives low-resolution results, and paid credits or subscriptions unlock high-resolution downloads.

item.title: Fliz
item.description:
Fliz focuses on one-click video creation. A user pastes a link or text, picks a style and voice, and Fliz writes a script if needed, assembles scenes, adds captions and music, and renders a video. The goal is a finished piece that can go straight to social media or a website.

Typical uses are turning blog posts into short videos, creating product videos for e-commerce, and producing news-style clips. Editing tools allow changes to visuals, text, and voices, and the platform supports many languages. Automation features generate videos in bulk from feeds.

item.title: Fotor
item.description:
Fotor covers everyday editing for people who do not want Photoshop. In the photo editor, you crop, adjust color and light, apply filters and effects, and retouch portraits by smoothing skin and removing blemishes. A collage maker and a design studio offer templates for social posts, posters, and cards. Everything works in a browser, with matching apps for phones and computers.

AI tools handle the harder steps. One-click enhancement improves exposure and sharpness, background removal makes cutouts, an object remover erases distractions, and an upscaler enlarges small pictures. Newer features include text-to-image generation, avatars, and generative fill for extending or changing parts of an image. Fotor also has an AI video editor for simple clips.

item.title: freebeat AI
item.description:
freebeat takes a different approach to video generation. A user uploads a track, and the platform produces visuals that follow the rhythm of the music, cutting and transforming on the beat. The result is a music-driven video that can be shared on social platforms.

Musicians use it to create lyric visuals and promotional clips without a video team. Creators use it for background visuals and short-form content. Styles and prompts guide the look, and users can adjust timing and effects.

item.title: Galileo AI
item.description:
Galileo AI was one of the early tools for turning a prompt into interface designs. You described a screen, such as a fitness app dashboard or a checkout page, and it produced a detailed, editable design with components, imagery, and layout, which could be copied into Figma and refined. It was popular with product designers and founders as a way to explore ideas and get past the blank canvas.

Google acquired Galileo AI and brought its team and technology into its own design-generation product, Stitch, which creates interfaces from text or images and exports to Figma and code. The standalone Galileo service was wound down as part of that move.

item.title: Hailuo AI
item.description:
Hailuo AI is the consumer face of video models from MiniMax, a Chinese AI company. You type a prompt or upload an image, and it generates a short video clip, with motion that many users find natural, including complex movement like dancing, sports, and camera moves. It gained a following among creators for the quality of its image-to-video results and its willingness to follow detailed prompts.

The platform offers tools for steering results. A subject reference feature keeps a character consistent across clips, camera controls guide movement, and different model versions trade speed for quality. It also generates images and offers voice and music features through MiniMax’s other models. An API lets developers use the video models in their own products.

item.title: Haiper
item.description:
Haiper launched as a fast, accessible video generator. Users typed a prompt or uploaded an image and received a short clip, with tools to extend videos, repaint areas, and animate stills. The company emphasized speed and iteration, aiming to let creators try many ideas quickly, and attracted attention as one of the more promising independent challengers to larger video model makers.

It could not keep pace with the rapid advances and heavy computing costs of video models. The company closed its consumer platform, and its founders moved to other roles, while its video models were acquired by another company that offers them through an API for enterprises. User projects hosted on the original platform were no longer accessible.

item.title: Ideogram
item.description:
Ideogram became known for solving a problem that frustrated early image generators: spelling. Ask most models for a poster that says “Grand Opening” and you get distorted letters, while Ideogram’s models usually produce clean, legible type in a chosen style. That makes it a practical choice for posters, book covers, t-shirt designs, logos, memes, and social media graphics, where words are part of the image.

It also performs well on general image generation, with strong prompt following across photorealistic, illustrated, and graphic design styles. Beyond generating from scratch, the apps include tools to remove backgrounds, erase objects, resize images for ads, and edit text layers. Teams can use private generation, shared libraries, and custom models, and a developer API provides the same models in other products.

item.title: Khroma
item.description:
Khroma starts by asking you to pick 50 colors you like. A neural network learns your tastes from those choices, then generates an endless stream of color combinations that match your style, shown as palettes, gradients, typography samples, and images. The aim is to make exploring color feel personal instead of random.

Designers use it to find inspiration for brand identities, websites, and illustrations. You can save favorite palettes, view them in different layouts, check color contrast, and search for combinations by a specific color. The interface is minimal and focused on discovery, and everything runs in the browser.

item.title: Kling AI
item.description: Kling is the AI video product from Kuaishou, the Chinese short-video company behind the Kwai app. Its models generate clips from a text description or a starting image, and they are well regarded for natural motion, realistic physics, and faces and bodies that stay coherent through a shot. When it first appeared, it was one of the strongest challengers to Western video tools, and it has stayed in the top group as the field has moved quickly.

item.title: Krea AI
item.description:
Krea became popular for its real-time canvas. As you type a prompt or sketch shapes, the image updates almost instantly, which turns generation into a live, exploratory process instead of waiting for each result. That immediacy suits designers and artists who iterate visually, adjusting composition and style through gestures rather than rewriting prompts.

The platform has expanded into a wide creative toolkit. It lets you generate images and video with a selection of models from different providers, upscale and enhance images with a strong emphasis on detail, edit existing pictures, and train custom styles from your own examples. Features such as pattern and logo generation, and tools for animating stills, appeal to designers and motion artists. Multiple models in one place make comparison easy.

item.title: Leonardo AI
item.description:
Leonardo.ai began as a tool for game developers who needed lots of consistent assets. Users generate images from text prompts with a choice of Leonardo’s own models and others, then refine them with inpainting, upscaling, and background removal. Fine-tuned models for characters, environments, items, and concept art made it popular with game artists, illustrators, and designers who care about a particular visual style.

Customization is a major draw. You can train your own models on a set of images to produce consistent characters or brand looks, use reference images to control composition and style, and draw on a canvas to guide generation. The platform has added video generation and animation of stills, along with an API for developers. A community feed lets users see what others are making and borrow prompts.

item.title: Luma Dream Machine
item.description: Dream Machine is how most people first used Luma AI’s video models. You describe a scene or upload a still image, and it produces a short clip with motion, lighting, and camera movement that tends to look cinematic. Luma started as a 3D capture company, which still shows in how well its video models handle depth and camera moves. People use it for concept videos, storyboards, social content, product shots, and b-roll when a shoot is not practical.

item.title: Luminar Neo
item.description: Luminar Neo is built for photographers who want strong results without a lot of manual work. Instead of slider-heavy workflows, it offers AI tools that do the hard parts in a click. Sky AI replaces or enhances skies, Relight AI changes the lighting in a scene using depth information, Portrait Bokeh AI creates background blur, and tools for skin, face, and body adjustments handle portraits. Generative tools can erase objects and expand the canvas.

item.title: MagicLight
item.description:
MagicLight is designed for narrative video. A user writes or pastes a story or script, chooses a style, and the platform produces scenes with characters, backgrounds, narration, and music. The aim is to let people who cannot animate create short animated stories and explainers.

It is used for children’s stories, educational content, social media series, and marketing videos. Features such as consistent characters across scenes help with storytelling, and editing tools allow changes to scenes and text before export.

item.title: Meshy
item.description:
Meshy makes 3D asset creation fast. You type a description or upload an image, and it generates a 3D mesh with textures in a minute or two. The results can be rotated, refined, and downloaded in common formats. Indie game developers, 3D printing hobbyists, product designers, and virtual world builders use it to produce props, characters, and environment pieces without modeling each from scratch.

The platform includes tools for the steps after generation. It can retexture a model from a prompt, remesh to adjust polygon counts and topology, and add skeletons and animations to characters. Plugins and an API connect it with Blender, Unity, Unreal Engine, Maya, and other tools, so assets can flow into existing pipelines. A library of community models provides starting points.

item.title: Mubert
item.description:
Mubert generates music in real time. You pick a mood, genre, or activity, such as focus, workout, or sleep, and it streams a continuous track that does not loop in an obvious way. Creators use it for background music in videos, streams, podcasts, and apps, and the royalty-free licensing makes it practical for online content.

Several products serve different needs. Mubert Render lets users create tracks of a chosen length from a text prompt or style, and a mobile app offers streaming for listening. An API allows developers to add generated music to games, fitness apps, and other products, delivering music that adapts to context. Artists can contribute sounds to the system, with revenue sharing for contributors.

item.title: NightCafe Studio
item.description:
NightCafe was one of the earliest AI art communities. It gives users access to various models, including Stable Diffusion variants, other leading generators, and its own options, so you can try different styles without separate accounts. You type a prompt, pick a model and style, and get images in seconds, then use tools to upscale, inpaint, or generate variations.

Community is a key part of the product. Users publish their creations, follow each other, join themed challenges, and vote, and a credit system rewards participation with free credits. Features like model training, text-to-video, and image-to-image extend what you can do, and prints on posters and canvases let people turn art into physical products. It is popular with hobbyists and casual creators.

item.title: Noodle Tomato
item.description:
Noodle Tomato targets faceless channel creators. A user enters a topic, and the tool writes a script, generates or selects visuals, adds a voiceover, and assembles a video that can be uploaded to YouTube. The aim is to make it possible to publish regularly with little production effort.

This style of content has drawn scrutiny. YouTube has policies against mass-produced, repetitive, or low-value videos, and channels that rely on automation without adding original value can lose monetization. Quality depends on editing, fact-checking, and a clear perspective.

item.title: Photoroom
item.description:
Photoroom grew from a background remover into a full product photography tool. Take a picture of a product on a table, and the app cuts it out cleanly, then places it on a white background, a color, or an AI-generated scene with realistic shadows and lighting. For small sellers on marketplaces like Etsy, eBay, and Shopify, that means professional-looking listings without a studio.

Other features expand the range. An AI backgrounds tool creates settings from a text description, an instant shadow and relight tool adds depth, and a magic retouch removes objects and blemishes. Templates in standard sizes speed up posts for social media and marketplaces. Batch editing handles whole catalogs, and an API lets platforms add the same processing to their own apps. Teams can share brand templates.

item.title: Pixlr
item.description:
Pixlr offers editing in a browser without installing software. Pixlr E is a more advanced editor with layers, masks, and adjustment tools that resemble Photoshop, while Pixlr X is a simpler editor for quick fixes, collages, and templates. It opens common image formats, including PSD files to an extent, and works on desktop and mobile browsers.

AI features handle the hard parts. Background removal makes cutouts in a click, an object eraser removes distractions, generative fill and expand add or extend content from a prompt, and automatic enhancement and retouching improve photos. An AI image generator and tools for creating designs from templates broaden what it can do. Pixlr is part of the Inmagine group, which also offers stock content.

item.title: PixVerse
item.description:
PixVerse turns prompts and images into video. Users describe a scene or upload a picture, choose a style, and receive a clip. Templates and effects support social content, and features like character consistency and lip sync help with storytelling.

The platform also provides editing, extension, and animation of still images, and offers apps for mobile and web. It is popular among social creators for fast, trend-driven formats.

PixVerse has a free tier with credits and paid plans. Output length and realism have limits, and rights depend on plan terms. Alternatives include Pika, Runway, Kling, Luma, and Higgsfield. PixVerse suits creators making quick AI videos.

item.title: Remove.bg
item.description:
Remove.bg made background removal fast and easy. You upload a photo, or drag it onto the page, and an AI model detects the foreground and returns the image with a transparent background in a few seconds. It handles people, products, animals, and cars, and it copes reasonably well with difficult edges like hair and fur. It is used for e-commerce product photos, profile pictures, ID photos, and design mockups.

The service extends beyond the website. Plugins connect it to Photoshop, Figma, and other tools, apps let you process images on a phone or desktop, and an API allows platforms to add automatic background removal at scale. Once the background is removed, you can add a solid color, a template, or another image. Bulk tools handle large catalogs. Remove.bg is owned by Canva.

item.title: Soundraw
item.description:
Soundraw makes custom background music for creators. You select parameters such as mood, genre, theme, tempo, and length, and the AI generates a number of options. You can then adjust the track in an editor, changing the intensity of different sections and instruments to match the pacing of a video, and download the result. This is more flexible than browsing a fixed stock library.

It’s aimed at content creators, marketers, filmmakers, and developers who need affordable music. The subscription offers unlimited downloads and a license for use on social platforms and in commercial projects, with protections against copyright claims on the creator’s own content. The tracks are made from music produced by in-house artists, and Soundraw positions the training data as licensed.

item.title: Suno
item.description: Suno made AI music accessible. You describe the song you want, such as an upbeat pop track about a road trip, or paste your own lyrics, and Suno produces complete songs with singing and instrumentation in under a minute. Users can choose styles and genres, extend and edit songs, create covers, and make instrumentals. It has been used for demos, background music, parody, and just for fun by people with no musical training.

item.title: ThumbnailCreator.com
item.description:
ThumbnailCreator targets one chore. A creator describes the thumbnail they want or uploads a frame from a video, and the tool produces several thumbnail options with text, backgrounds, and subjects arranged to catch attention.

Because thumbnails strongly affect click rates, creators iterate on them often. A generator that makes variations lets them test ideas without opening a design program each time.

Independent information is limited. ThumbnailCreator has a free tier and paid plans. Alternatives include Canva, Photoroom, VidIQ and TubeBuddy thumbnail tools, Midjourney, and hiring a designer. ThumbnailCreator suits YouTubers who make many thumbnails.

item.title: Tripo3D
item.description:
Tripo focuses on speed and consistency. Enter a description or upload an image, and it generates a 3D model in seconds to a minute, with options for style and level of detail. The models are meant to be usable in games, animation, 3D printing, and e-commerce, and the platform provides downloads in common formats like GLB, FBX, and OBJ.

Features go beyond the initial generation. Tools can create cleaner topology for animation, generate or replace textures from a prompt, add skeletons so characters can be posed, and apply animations. A segmentation option separates a model into parts for editing. An API and integrations with Blender, Unity, Unreal, and other applications fit it into creative pipelines, and a community library offers starting points.

item.title: Udio
item.description:
Udio produces music with an emphasis on audio quality and handling of lyrics. You describe a song or supply lyrics, and Udio generates clips that you can extend into full tracks, remix, and edit section by section. Users liked it for realistic vocals and for the control it gives over structure, and it has been used for songwriting ideas, demos, and entertainment.

Its path changed after legal disputes with major record labels. Udio reached licensing agreements with some labels and moved toward a platform where creation and sharing happen inside the service, often described as a walled garden, with limits on downloading tracks. Plans to build tools around licensed music mean terms can continue to change, and the experience differs from earlier versions, which let users download freely.

item.title: Uizard
item.description:
Uizard is a design tool built for speed and accessibility. You can upload a photo of a sketch or a screenshot of an existing app and have it converted into an editable design, or describe a screen in text and let the AI generate a layout. A library of templates, components, and themes helps non-designers build presentable prototypes for products, websites, and apps.

Collaboration features let teams comment and iterate, and prototypes can be linked into clickable flows. An Autodesigner feature creates multi-screen designs from a prompt, and the AI can generate color themes from an image. It’s popular with founders, product managers, and consultants who need quick mockups to communicate ideas.

item.title: VidFlux
item.description:
VidFlux takes a still image and brings it to life. A user uploads a photo, optionally describes the motion, and the tool generates a short video with movement such as camera pans, flowing hair, or moving water.

Marketers use it to give product photos life in ads and social feeds, and creators animate portraits and artwork. The clips are short and quality varies with the image.

Independent information is limited. VidFlux has a free tier and paid plans. Alternatives include Runway, Pika, Luma, Kling, and PixVerse. VidFlux suits creators animating still images.

item.title: Wan Video
item.description:
Wan generates video from descriptions. Users provide a prompt or an image, and the model produces a clip with motion and detail. Alibaba has released several versions, including open-weight models that run on local hardware and have attracted a large community of tools and fine-tunes.

Creators and filmmakers use Wan for text-to-video, image-to-video, and editing tasks, through hosted sites and through open-source workflows such as ComfyUI. Open availability makes it a base for research and custom pipelines.

item.title: X-Pilot AI
item.description:
X-Pilot AI is aimed at teaching content. A user uploads a document or slide deck, and the tool builds a video with scenes, narration, and animations. Avatars can present the material, and editors can adjust text and visuals.

It helps trainers who have written material but lack time or skills to produce video. Videos can be translated into other languages.

Independent information is limited. X-Pilot AI has a free tier and paid plans. Alternatives include Synthesia, HeyGen, Colossyan, Elai.io, and Pictory. X-Pilot AI suits course creators turning documents into video.
